name.ja: アルバート・セービン

overview.en: Albert Sabin was a Polish-American medical researcher who developed the oral polio vaccine that became the primary tool in the global eradication of poliomyelitis.

early_life.en: Born in Bialystok, Poland, he emigrated to the United States as a teenager and studied medicine at New York University.

impact.en: His oral polio vaccine, easier to administer than the Salk injectable vaccine, became the standard worldwide and was instrumental in nearly eradicating polio globally.

event.en: Developed the oral polio vaccine using attenuated live virus
Oral polio vaccine tested successfully on millions in the Soviet Union
Oral polio vaccine licensed for use in the United States

description.en: Live attenuated vaccine administered orally, enabling mass immunization campaigns worldwide

text.en: A scientist who is also a human being cannot rest while knowledge which might be used to reduce suffering rests on a shelf.
